To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phonon and electronic properties of Si nanoparticles can be studied in situ by Raman and electron energy loss spectroscopy.
the Raman scattering spectra of ultra thin Si layers show size-dependent features that are due to the relaxation of the conservation of the k-vector condition.

the phonon density-of-states of Si nanoparticles is strongly dependent on the size and shape of the nanoparticles and that the electronic transitions in Si nanoparticles are shifted to higher energies with decreasing size of the nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of silicon nanoparticles in the size range of 1 to 100 nm and with the study of their electronic and vibrational properties.
the development of a new method for the preparation of thin films and nanostructures by sputtering in ultra high vacuum.
the synthesis and characterization of Si quantum dots and their electronic and vibrational properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electronic and vibrational properties of Si nanoparticles can be studied in situ by Raman and EELS spectroscopy.
the electronic properties of the Si nanoparticles are not affected by the size of the particles, but rather by the nature of the buffer layer and the crystalline state of the particles.
the electronic properties of Si quantum dots are not very different from the bulk Si properties, whereas the phonon properties are very different from the phonon density states of bulk Si.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic and vibrational properties of Si nanoparticles are strongly size-dependent.
we can detect the size-dependencies in both the electronic and vibrational properties of Si quantum dots by using the electron and light energy loss spectroscopies, respectively.
the phonon and the electronic spectra are sensitive to the size and the degree of order of the Si nanoparticles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vibrational and electronic properties of nanoparticles can be studied in situ using Raman spectroscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy.
the Raman spectra of the crystalline Si quantum dots are not a superposition of the spectra of bulk crystalline Si and Si amorphous.
in situ measurements of electronic and vibrational properties of nanostructures are a powerful tool for the study of size effects in nanostructures.
